pr.title: Phase 1b: add native domain and mailbox administration
pr.body:
The replacement web panel can now create, update and delete domains and mailboxes through explicit native management commands and REST endpoints. It adds storage limits, write-only password resets, administrator roles, and searchable lists capped at 100 results per response.

Native authorization enforces domain ownership, protects persisted server-administrator accounts from domain administrators, and prevents deletion of the current account/domain. Existing business persistence validates names, duplicates and quotas and invalidates authentication caches. The responsive panel confirms destructive actions and recovers its sign-in state after credential revocation.

Validation for head `7fa4f1375a799faae27dcb8fa5ab9ee8a619a0e1`:
- Release x64, GCC, Clang, all four installed-server database jobs and installer publication passed.
- NUnit: 1,315 tests per backend. Compact/PostgreSQL/MySQL: 1,205 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 76 skipped. SQL Server Express: 1,206 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 75 skipped.
- Each database job also passed 26 DNS + 83 HTTP/security + 2 HTTPS + 69 native assertions (180 total) and the expanded browser workflows. HTTP and browser tests use explicit fixtures; native tests exercise each real service/database backend.
- Disposable Hyper-V VM: the same 180 management assertions, 2 additional pipe identity assertions, and browser checks passed. Existing account/domain categories: 24 total, 22 passed, 0 failed, 2 inconclusive. The original VM executable, database, configuration and checkpoint were restored.
- All runtime tests/previews ran only in the VM or CI. The development host was used for editing, static inspection and compilation.

Updates the REST contract, CI inventory, roadmap, requirements and shared agent handoff. Names/addresses remain immutable; advanced administration, self-service, certificate lifecycle, Defender integration, production hosting and PHP retirement remain separate work. Lists filter existing business collections in memory; database-side pagination remains a capacity follow-up.

This PR completes only the current authorized slice. Wait for maintainer confirmation before the next task, and do not merge without an explicit instruction.

+Domain and mailbox lists accept `search` (case-insensitive substring), `offset` (default 0),
+and `limit` (default 50, maximum 100). Responses contain `items`, `total`, `offset`, `limit`.
+Unknown/duplicate HTTP filters and out-of-range native pagination are rejected. Collections are
+loaded using existing business objects and filtered in memory; pagination bounds the response,
+not database work. Indexed database-side paging remains a capacity follow-up.
+
+Domain POST accepts `name` (required), `active`, `maxMessageSizeKB`, `maxSizeMB`,
+`maxAccountSizeMB`. PATCH accepts the same fields except `name`; domain administrators may
+change only `active` on their own domain. Names/addresses are immutable in this slice.
+Mailbox POST accepts `address` and a nonempty `password` (required), `active`, `maxSizeMB`,
+and `level` (0 user, 1 domain administrator, 2 server administrator). PATCH accepts all except
+`address`. Defaults follow the native business objects; the panel explicitly creates active
+objects and normal-user mailboxes. Numeric sizes are nonnegative 32-bit integers; 0 means
+unlimited subject to domain policy. Names/addresses, duplicate aliases/lists and quotas use the
+shared native persistence validation. Invalid/duplicate/quota failures return 422 without
+echoing submitted credentials. Infrastructure failures return 503.
+
+Domain administrators cannot create/promote server administrators or read the detail, reset,
+demote, disable or delete an existing server administrator account. Scoped listings show only
+basic identity/status/role/quota information for these accounts. They cannot change their own role.
+Mailbox users have no access to these administrative operations; account self-service remains
+future work. The active account and its owning domain cannot be deleted by that session (409).
+Deletion uses existing cascading persistence and permanently removes dependent mail data;
+the panel confirms the impact first. There is no new undo facility.
+
+Passwords are write-only, hashed using the configured native password hasher, and never included
+in views. Omit `password` on PATCH to preserve it; blank passwords are rejected. AD-backed
+password changes are rejected and must be made in the directory. No AD provisioning is added.
+The next request reauthenticates and observes password, role, active-state or deletion changes.
+The panel ends the session after changing its own password/role or disabling its own account.
+
 DNSBL creation accepts `Active` (boolean), `DNSHost`, `ExpectedResult`, `RejectMessage`
 (strings), and `Score` (integer 0..10000). All five fields are required. PATCH accepts a subset.

issue.body:
The web panel can now manage domain aliases, distribution lists, posting settings and list members through explicit native commands and REST endpoints. It adds searchable, paginated lists, activation controls, member editing and deletion, and confirmation for consequential posting-policy changes.

Server administrators can manage every domain; domain administrators can manage only their own. The native dispatcher checks domain/list/object ownership, validates single addresses and allowed fields before persistence, rejects duplicate members and direct self-targets, and uses existing quota/collision rules and cache invalidation. New aliases and lists default disabled; lists default members-only with SMTP authentication required. No database schema, web SQL or COM backend dependency is added.

Posting modes preserve the existing engine's envelope-sender semantics. Required SMTP authentication does not bind the envelope sender to the authenticated identity; the UI and REST contract explain this, including the domain-sender mode's treatment of nonexistent mailboxes. Public posting and authentication settings remain explicit administrator choices.

Validation for head `3e83eaddfd2f23daf7255ae17bf22a67e3bc8b70`:
- Native Release and .NET builds passed; development-host compilation only.
- Disposable Hyper-V VM: 26 DNS + 132 HTTP/security + 2 HTTPS + 152 native assertions passed (312 total), plus 2 separate pipe identity assertions.
- Native tests include real SMTP RCPT probes for alias activation/deletion, all four posting modes, required authentication and member-cache invalidation. They send no DATA, queue no messages and perform no external delivery.
- All 15 selected existing distribution-list/alias-name regression tests passed with zero failures or inconclusive results.
- VM browser fixtures passed alias/list/member CRUD, activation and deletion confirmations/cancellation, password/session regression workflows and mobile layout checks.
- The control-character validation regression was reproduced in the VM before its fix. Original VM server/database/configuration and the temporary checkpoint were restored.
- CI passed: Release x64, GCC, Clang, all four installed-server database jobs and installer publication. Each backend passed all 312 management assertions and the expanded browser workflows.
- NUnit: 1,315 tests per backend. Compact/PostgreSQL/MySQL: 1,205 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 76 skipped. Express: 1,206 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 34 inconclusive, 75 skipped. Totals match the previous baseline.

Updates the API contract, CI inventory, README, roadmap, requirements and shared agent handoff, including merged PR #35 and this authorized next slice. Renaming alias/list addresses, bulk membership operations, complete graph-cycle validation, indexed database pagination and the rest of Phase 1b remain separate work.

Pause for maintainer review after this PR; do not start the next task or merge without explicit instruction.
